page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 6 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression are positioned in the bottom 25% of tested servers. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including the stress-ng multi-core test, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU score, fall within the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests, such as uncached large-block reads at 71.39 GB/sec and writes at 43.14 GB/sec, also demonstrate average performance.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is the contrast between its weak single-threaded execution speeds and its robust memory capacity. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density allows organizations to run memory-intensive applications without paying for excess CPU cores. Lacking local storage, it requires network storage configuration. This profile is appropriate for workloads such as in-memory databases like Redis, caching layers, mid-sized database management systems, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
